data.name: Armando
data.gender_notes: Armando is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The man who works, the one who serves, the soldier, the brave one, the powerful one. The name Armando carries the meaning “Soldier, Worker” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Armando usually hope their child will grow to embody soldier, worker and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.etymology: Armando belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Soldier, Worker.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Armando total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

in_hebrew.name: ערמנד
in_hebrew.meaning: אוהב האדם, חברי, נאמן, יקר, אהוב
in_hebrew.long_meaning: ערמנד הוא שם נראה, שאול מהלטינית ומשמעותו 'אוהב האדם, חברי, נאמן, יקר, אהוב'. בספר בראשית, 5:1, נאמר 'וישא ער, ויאמר, ער, יצלח, לכל אשר יעשה, ושמו ער'. פירוש השם, 'ער', בעברית, 'להיות ראש, ' תמיד, 'להיות נאמן'. המשמעות הזאת, 'אוהב האדם', 'חברי', 'נאמן', 'יקר', 'אהוב', נמצאת, גם בשם, 'ערמנד', בפשטות, 'אוהב האדם'.

in_greek.name: Αρμάνδος
in_greek.meaning: αγαπητής ανθρώπου, φίλος, πιστός, πολυπόθητος, αγαπητός
in_greek.long_meaning: Ο Άρμάνδος είναι όνομα που φαίνεται, που προέρχεται από την αλαμανική γλώσσα και σημαίνει 'αγαπητής ανθρώπου, φίλος, πιστός, πολυπόθητος, αγαπητός'. Στην Καινή Διαθήκη, ο Άρμάνδος είναι ένα από τα ονόματα που απαντάται μόνο μία φορά, στο εβδομήντο εβδομαδάριο του 1ου Κορίνθιο, 4:16. Ο Άρμάνδος είναι επίσης ένα από τα ονόματα των αποστόλων, που αναφέρεται στο εβδομήντο εβδομαδάριο του 1ου Κορίνθιο, 12:28.

in_latin.name: Armando
in_latin.meaning: amans hominem, amicus, fidelis, carus, dilectus
in_latin.long_meaning: Armando est nomen apparentem, quod ab Alemanica lingua provenit et significat 'amans hominem, amicus, fidelis, carus, dilectus'. In Novo Testamento, Armando est unus ex nominibus quae tantummodo semel apparet, in septimo hebdomadario 1 Corintiorum, 4:16. Armando est etiam unus ex nominibus apostolorum, qui referitur in septimo hebdomadario 1 Corintiorum, 12:28.

in_english.name: Armando
in_english.meaning: loves man, friend, faithful, dear, beloved
in_english.long_meaning: The name Armando is seen, derived from the Latin language and meaning 'loves man, friend, faithful, dear, beloved'. In the Bible, Armando is one of the names that appears only once, in the seventh week of 1 Corinthians, 4:16. Armando is also one of the names of the apostles, which is referred to in the seventh week of 1 Corinthians, 12:28. The name Armando is associated with the personality traits of being a loving person, a good friend, faithful, dear, and beloved. In Christian tradition, Armando is a symbol of love and devotion to God and to others.

data.cultural_impact: The name Armando is of Latin origin, derived from the Roman name Harold or Hermann. It was popular in medieval Europe and became common in Spanish, Italian, Portuguese, and Filipino cultures. In Spanish and Italian cultures, it is also associated with the military, and the name has been borne by several military leaders and soldiers.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Armando holds a deeper spiritual significance as it derives from the Latin words "arma" (weapons) and "manus" (hands), representing the idea of using one's God-given abilities to protect, serve, and defend others. This name embodies the Christian values of courage, strength, and selflessness, making it an inspiring and meaningful name for a Christian child. It serves as a reminder that every individual has a unique role to play in God's greater plan and that strength and bravery come from relying on God's guidance and protection.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Armando, meaning "soldier of man," is a name that symbolizes courage and dedication in the service of humanity. It reminds us of the call to be warriors for love, justice, and compassion in our everyday lives.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Armando was a 16th century Italian painter. The name Armando carried significant spiritual weight in that era.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name Armando remains relevant in modern Christian society, representing a bridge between traditional Biblical values and contemporary life. It is widely discussed on digital platforms and continues to be a popular choice for families seeking meaningful Christian names.

name_in_real_life.story: Mary Armando, a minister in Dublin, Ireland, shares that their name Armando meaning "Soldier, Worker" has been a constant source of inspiration, guiding them to serve others and live according to Christian values.
